content:
I am currently finishing my notes "Exploring Formalisation. A Primer in Human-Readable Mathematics in Lean 3 with Examples from Simplicial Topology" (which will soon-ish be published in a Springer book series).

The goal is to give mathematicians an introduction into straightforward and human-readable formalisation of ordinary pen-and-paper mathematics -- starting from first-year material and leading to recent research topics.

I am aware that the focus on human-readability leads to code that looks different from the "usual" Lean library code, but I believe that this kind of readability has many benefits for mathematicians. Moreover, in order to not delay this project, I still went with Lean 3 (and the Lean 3 mathlib). Once mathlib is ported to Lean 4, it should also be easy to adapt the book. Many of the main principles are independent of the concrete proof assistant anyway.

You can find the draft pdf and the Lean source code at

https://loeh.app.uni-regensburg.de/mapa/

Feedback is very welcome! (in particular, on Chapter 1, as I am obviously no Lean expert, but just an end-user :) )
